summary: AstroHealth is a health monitoring tool for astronauts on long missions. It shows heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, temperature, sleep, and mood on a single screen. A 3D body map points to the organ that needs attention. Trend charts show changes over the days. Our demo simulates a 942-day mission to Mars. It uses data from multiple real missions, including NASA open data. It runs in the browser, on a phone or a computer. Our goal is simple. No one in space should feel alone with their health.
details:
What it does. AstroHealth turns raw health readings into clear visual signals. Each crew member has a profile. The body map highlights systems at risk. Trend charts compare the last days against a personal baseline. The mission view shows Earth, Mars, the ship, and the current signal delay.

Benefits. Astronauts can take immediate action without having to wait for input from Earth. Mission control receives the same information once the signal arrives. This same concept can be useful for people who are far away from a doctor on Earth. Data can be captured using simple IoT solutions and by leveraging ARCHeR.

Tools. Next.js, React, TypeScript, Three.js for 3D. Python for data processing. NASA OSDR (Inspiration4 blood panels), JPL Horizons for Mars positions, DONKI for space weather. Deployed on Vercel as an installable web app.

Creativity. We built the story of a full Mars mission. Day by day, the data changes with distance, isolation, and radiation events.

Factors we considered. Communication delay. Small screens. Calm design under stress. Honest use of simulated data. No medical claims.
